title: Post error budget burn summaries into incident Slack channels
author: Miles Thornton
release_notes: Incident Bot now posts periodic error budget burn summaries into active incident channels (with dashboard + runbook links) to make budget impact visible during mitigation.
description:
Motivation: during recent incidents we’ve had a consistent gap between (a) what responders are doing (rollbacks, throttling, routing fallbacks) and (b) whether those actions are actually stopping error budget burn for the impacted tier/route. This PR adds an incident-bot capability to post budget burn summaries into the incident Slack channel while an incident is active, with deep links to the tiered SLO dashboards and the budget exhaustion runbook.

What this does: when an incident channel is created/linked (or when the bot sees an incident transition into ACTIVE), incident-bot starts a periodic reporter (default: every 15 minutes) that posts a short “budget status” message. The reporter is scoped to the incident’s impacted service(s) and tier (Hosted/Dedicated) when available; if no tier is set it defaults to Hosted and includes an explicit warning in the message. Messages are posted as replies in a single thread to avoid channel spam.

Budget source: calls the internal Budget Status API exposed by the control plane (GET /internal/slo/budget/status) with service + tier + window (30d) and pulls (1) budget remaining %, (2) current burn rate signals (multi-window), and (3) top contributing SLI class (5xx, timeouts, streaming disconnects, latency). If the API is unreachable or the service is not onboarded, the bot posts a one-time “budget unavailable” message and stops retrying for 1 hour.

Message format (example):
- Error budget (Hosted / gateway.chat.stream): 62% remaining (30d)
- Burn signals: 2h/30m = 4.8x, 6h/1h = 2.1x (at-risk)
- Dominant SLI burn: streaming_disconnect_server
- Links: SLO dashboard (tier=Hosted, region=us-east-1), Burn-rate panel, Runbook: Error budget exhaustion response

Links: dashboard + runbook URLs are constructed from a small config map so we can standardize naming without hardcoding Grafana folder IDs in code. The runbook link points to the oncall Confluence page for “Error budget exhaustion response”.

Safety/anti-noise: (1) only posts while incident status is ACTIVE/INVESTIGATING/MITIGATING, (2) posts into a single Slack thread, (3) suppresses posts when nothing changed materially (budget remaining delta < 0.5% AND no burn window crosses thresholds), (4) hard cap of 16 posts per incident per 24h, (5) Dedicated incidents: the bot never includes customer identifiers, pool names, or tenant IDs; it only includes tier + service + region.

Rollout plan: behind feature flag ENABLE_BUDGET_BURN_SUMMARIES (default off). Initial enablement will be limited to #incidents-* channels created by the SRE oncall rotation and only for the gateway + routing services pilot. We can widen once we’re confident in noise levels and SLI correctness.

Testing: adds unit tests for burn signal classification, message formatting, and Slack threading; adds a lightweight integration test harness that replays an incident lifecycle event stream and asserts posting cadence + suppression behavior.

Operational notes: reporter uses a per-incident in-memory state to track last-posted snapshot (budget remaining + burn windows + dominant class). This state resets if the bot restarts; in that case the bot posts a fresh summary immediately on restart (still threaded).

Docs: updated incident-bot README with configuration keys and a short troubleshooting section ("budget API 404", "missing dashboard mapping", and "why didn’t it post?").
commits: Add BudgetStatusClient (control plane) with retry/backoff + circuit breaker
Incident lifecycle hook: start/stop budget reporter based on incident status
Slack: post budget summaries as threaded replies + suppression logic
Add dashboard/runbook link builder + config validation
Unit tests for burn window parsing and message formatting
review_conversation:
Logan Wright: Can we avoid hammering the control plane during big incidents? We’ve had Slack bots accidentally DoS internal APIs before. Miles Thornton: Added per-incident cadence cap + jitter, plus a circuit breaker that backs off for 60m after 5 consecutive failures. Also added client-side caching for identical requests within 2 minutes.

Aisha Bello: The message should call out which SLI class is burning (timeouts vs disconnects) so responders pick the right mitigations. Also please link the budget exhaustion runbook. Miles Thornton: Updated the payload parsing to surface dominant_class and wired the Confluence runbook link into the message. Added tests for classification mapping.

Nadia Rahman: For Dedicated, ensure we never leak customer/pool identifiers. Also what happens if tier is missing? Miles Thornton: Dedicated path now rejects any incident context fields that look like tenant/pool IDs (sanity check) and message only includes tier/service/region. If tier is missing, we default to Hosted but emit "tier not set" warning in the first post so responders fix the incident metadata.

Sean Gallagher: Threading is required; we can’t spam incident channels every 15 minutes. Also add suppression when burn windows are stable. Miles Thornton: Implemented single-thread posting keyed by incident ID, plus suppression based on delta thresholds and burn-window threshold crossings. Added a hard cap of 16 posts/24h.

Sean Gallagher: Approve after the suppression logic lands + docs. Sean Gallagher: Approved.

Aisha Bello: Approved with the Dedicated redaction change. Aisha Bello: Approved.
